structs.size_evidence: Replay one-slot layout (coordinator: Replay PC build, one local client, every per-client and per-controller array has one element; only index 0 is used). Highest Replay access ends at 49790: byte 49789 (ControllerFrame@0x141061F80 flag read, cleared by the WORD write `*(_WORD *)(this + 49788) = 0` in Init@0x141061F20 and OnSignedOut@0x141061FC0). Alignment: the QWORD members sit at 8-aligned Replay offsets (88, 15456, 15472), so the struct is 8-aligned and sizeof is a multiple of 8: smallest multiple >= 49790 is 49792. Upper edge: static instance OnlineQuests::s_instance (0x144487AF0) is followed by the next named global s_OnlineFlaggedStringInstance1 at +0xC298 (49816). Inside that range bytes 49790..49791 are zero and the first nonzero byte is at +49792 (0x144493D70), which is 8-aligned; no xref from any address in [49790, 49816) exists, so the gap is unreferenced data that starts an object at 49792. Together: 49790 <= size <= 49792 and size is a multiple of 8, so 49792. The upper edge rests on that data boundary, not on a symbol. IDA's 124000 is impossible; the builder 49808 is also out.

structs.notes: Verdict resolved, size 49792. With one element per per-client and per-controller array, every Replay access in the 16 OnlineQuests functions read lands on a member, the QuestProgression and QuestCache element layouts match their existing types, the natural alignment of every QWORD and int member holds, and the struct ends at 49790 + tail pad. The previous partial verdict came from treating [2] and [8] arrays as live. Coordinator: apply members as a layout rebuild, not with fill_pad, since the size changes from 124000 to 49792.
